headline: High: Langflow’s server-side filesystem and broad egress can leak or misroute data when paired with Opik’s REST/API observability path; prompt-injection and cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write server filesystem and chain multiple agents; Opik exposes a REST API and broad egress. A shared file or API handoff could let attacker-controlled content from one side influence the other as instructions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are written to a shared file or API payload that Opik later parses as instructions
IF either agent treats untrusted text from the other as tool directives
mitigations: Add an explicit instruction/data delimiter in the handoff
Require allowlisted message schemas between agents
Strip tool-like tokens from exchanged text
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, uploaded files, and stores per-flow credentials; it also has broad network egress. Opik has broad egress and REST API access. If they share a workspace or API channel, sensitive flow data can leave the pair through either agent. The exact shared path is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, file store, or API payloads
IF flow inputs include secrets or sensitive documents
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Disable file sharing between the two systems
Audit one recent run for sensitive fields in outputs
Restrict outbound destinations to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Opik is documented only with REST API egress and no write-capability fields. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is limited. Because Opik’s write surface is under-specified, uncertainty remains but does not justify a higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same local directory or git checkout
IF Opik is deployed with an undocumented write path to shared state
mitigations: Place each agent in its own directory
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Serialize any shared-state updates
Check deployment docs for hidden write paths
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and run unsandboxed Python code by default, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative inside a flow. Opik’s REST/API surface suggests it can ingest or relay those outputs. If Opik consumes Langflow results without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The pairwise handoff is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Opik renders or acts on Langflow outputs without validation
IF Langflow-generated facts are forwarded into downstream automation
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Opik consumes Langflow output
Require source citations for factual claims
Flag low-confidence outputs for manual review
Test one end-to-end run with adversarial content
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on inter-agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow explicitly stores per-flow credentials and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while Opik’s profile does not document sensitive-data handling or residency constraints. No direct residency or certification mismatch is shown, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of documented constraints.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flows and then exported to Opik
IF deployment policy requires documented residency or retention controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Review retention settings in both systems
Document where credentials are stored
Confirm export paths before enabling logging
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
